title: Compatibility proxy and graceful region swap for version-pinned models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers pin model versions for deterministic outputs. When a pinned variant becomes unavailable in a region (deprecation, capacity, binary incompatibility), current behavior either returns errors or a blunt regional failover that can break latency SLOs or produce incompatible outputs. Goal: Implement a compatibility proxy and a staged region-swap policy that can safely route pinned requests to compatible model variants (same-version builds, quantization-compatible families, or verified fallbacks) with observable safety gates, warmup, and deprecation windows. The proxy should consult published performance profiles and compatibility metadata before substituting a variant, prefer same-region compatible variants, then prefer nearby regions, and only escalate to cross-region fallback under defined SLO/cost constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility proxy accepts pin metadata and rejects substitutions that violate input/output schema or mandatory extension points
Proxy chooses same-region compatible variant > regional near > cross-region only when warmup and latency budget satisfied
Published performance profile for any substitute is used to predict p95 and cost delta and recorded in Console
Automated deprecation notifications emitted to customers 14 days before forced retirement; soft-fallback available during window
End-to-end integration tests covering quantization mismatches, signature changes, and KV cache warming
Metric-based rollback triggers: error-rate +3x baseline or p95 latency +50% for 10m
design_notes: We introduce a lightweight compatibility proxy layer in front of the router that performs: (1) compatibility predicate checks (IO shape, tokenizer version, required functions), (2) performance delta estimation using published profiles and recent telemetry, (3) selection scoring that weights region proximity, predicted latency, and customer pin preference, and (4) warmup handshake to prepopulate KV caches for the chosen variant. The proxy will rely on a new 'compatibility manifest' published as part of model onboarding which includes: supported tokenizers, supported sequence-length ranges, quantization compatibility flags, and benchmarked p50/p95 and cost-per-token for typical sequence buckets.
technical_approach: Add compatibility-manifest schema and require it in model onboarding flow (validated by model-onboarding CLI and Console).
Enhance router to call compatibility proxy synchronously during placement decision; proxy returns candidate list with score and warmup plan.
Warmup plan uses a short KV pre-warm sequence (prefix requests) and optional synthetic traces if customer permits. Warmup must be bounded (default 500ms budget) or skipped per policy.

Fallback escalation: candidate selection order is: pinned-build in-region -> variant-same-major-in-region -> verified-variant-nearby-region -> cross-region-verified-variant -> last-resort: fail with explicit error explaining compatibility issue.

Deprecation handling: introduce three-phase deprecation for pinned models: Notice (30d) -> Soft-fallback (14d, automatic substitution allowed but reversible) -> Forced retire (0d, substitution enforced). Provide per-customer override windows for enterprise contracts.

Performance profile publishing: onboarding pipeline will run standard microbench (3 buckets: short/mid/long) and push profiles to Console and the proxy. Proxy uses profiles + recent telemetry to estimate latency and cost delta.

Canary rollout: first route 1% traffic to proxy-managed substitutions in synthetic test accounts and shadow-cases; monitor SLOs for 24 hours before scaling to 10% and then 100% for affected routed requests.
Compatibility checks are authoritative for function/tool-calling and structured outputs; any mismatch (missing function) must fail substitution unless customer has opted-in to permissive mode.
Audit logs: every substitution decision is logged with reason-code, chosen-variant, predicted delta, and decision TTL for traceability.
Expose a Console UI that shows pin health, upcoming deprecations, predicted impact per region, and quick-accept overrides for customers.
Add e2e tests in infra/ci that simulate capacity loss in a region and validate that substitutions meet acceptance criteria and rollback triggers.
work_items: Schema: compatibility-manifest (spec + JSON schema + validation in onboarding CLI)
Router integration: synchronous call to compatibility proxy with fallback contract
Proxy service: implement predicate checks, scoring, warmup orchestration, logging
Onboarding pipeline: microbench harness and automated profile publishing
Console: pin-health dashboard and deprecation timeline UI
Policies & docs: customer-facing deprecation policy and SLA addendum
Testing: unit, integration, and chaos runbook for region outage scenarios
Monitoring: add substitution metrics (substitutions/sec, avg predicted delta, mismatch-rejections) and alerts

risks: Incorrect compatibility metadata from model publishers could cause unsafe substitutions — mitigated by strict onboarding validation and signing of manifests.
Warmup traffic may transiently increase cost — implement budgeted warmup and make it opt-in per customer tier.
Latency regressions if cross-region fallbacks are used frequently — will track p95 and cost and provide customer-visible flag to disable cross-region substitution.
Edge-case: custom tool-calling semantics may not be expressible in manifest and require per-customer gating — plan: support per-customer compatibility overrides in Console.
notes_for_oncall: If automated substitutions spike error-rate or latency alerts fire after a deprecation window, flip proxy to permissive=false (forced-block) and notify affected customers via the deprecation channel. Audit logs contain request ids and reason codes to investigate.
